Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

the top of phrase

the top, middle, bottom, end or rest of a thing

also at the top of, top of the tree, top of the mountain, the middle of, in the middle of the night, the bottom of, at the foot of, the end of, the far end of, the rest of, the beginning of, at first light, a great part of, most of

classical

Liv. 2.13.11: in summā Sacrā viā

summus, summa, summum

adjective, agreeing with the noun for the whole

the top of: the top of the tree, the top of the hill

Latin says “the highest tree” for “the top of the tree”: in summā arbore, at the top of the tree; summus mōns, the top of the mountain. So with every word here: the part is an adjective agreeing with the whole, not a noun with a genitive.

Other words

  • medius, media, medium — the middle of: the middle of the night, of the road

    adjective, agreeing with its noun · classical · Gell. 3.2.2: ā mediā nocte ad proximam mediam noctem

    media nox, the middle of the night, midnight; in mediā viā, in the middle of the road (see centre).

  • īmus, īma, īmum — the bottom of, the foot of

    adjective, agreeing with its noun · classical · Liv. 40.22.2: in īmīs collibus

    in īmīs collibus, at the foot of the hills.

  • extrēmus, extrēma, extrēmum — the end of, the far edge of

    adjective, agreeing with its noun · classical · Catull. 11.2: in extrēmōs … Indōs

    The farthest part of a place, or the last of a time; ultimus is used the same way.

  • reliquus, reliqua, reliquum — the rest of

    adjective, agreeing with its noun · classical · Liv. 21.33.1: agmen reliquum

    agmen reliquum, the rest of the column; for the others besides those named, cēterī (see the rest).

  • prīmus, prīma, prīmum — the beginning of, the front of

    adjective, agreeing with its noun · also used · classical · Liv. 21.33.1: prīmā deinde lūce

    prīmā lūce, at first light.

  • magna (maxima) pars + gen. — a great part of, most of

    noun phrase, with the genitive of the whole · also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 1.1: magna pars vītae

    Here the genitive is right, because pars is a noun (see most).

  • medium, mediī n. + gen. — the middle of (a noun with a genitive)

    also used · classical · Ov. F. 4.549: noctis erat medium

    (vōx plērumque poētica: Ov.; in ōrātiōne solūtā posterior)

    Poetry and later prose; in plain speech say media nox.

Examples

  • Fēlēs in summā arbore sedet.

    The cat is sitting at the top of the tree.composed

  • Jam media nox est; dormī.

    It’s the middle of the night now; go to sleep.composed

  • in summā Sacrā viā fuit posita virgō īnsidēns equō

    at the top of the Sacred Way was set up a girl sitting on a horseLiv. 2.13.11

  • modicus prīmō labor in īmīs collibus fuit

    at first the toil at the foot of the hills was moderateLiv. 40.22.2

  • prīmā deinde lūce castra mōta et agmen reliquum incēdere coepit

    then at first light the camp was struck, and the rest of the column began to moveLiv. 21.33.1

  • quī inde ā mediā nocte ad proximam mediam noctem … nātī sunt

    those born from one midnight to the nextGell. 3.2.2

  • sīve in extrēmōs penetrābit Indōs

    whether he makes his way to the farthest IndiansCatull. 11.2

  • noctis erat medium placidīque silentia somnī

    it was the middle of the night, and the silence of peaceful sleepOv. F. 4.549

  • magna pars vītae ēlābitur male agentibus, maxima nihil agentibus, tōta vīta aliud agentibus

    a great part of life slips away from those who do wrong, most of it from those who do nothing, the whole of it from those who do something elseSen. Ep. 1.1

See also top, bottom, centre, the rest, summit, most, part, half, whole.
